## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Nowadays attempting to retrieve a control in a negative index returns `undefined` (due to underlying usage of native `Array`).

Issue Number: #44642

## What is the new behavior?

Similar to the ES2021 [`Array.prototype.at()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/at), support negative integers as indices:
```ts
formArray.at(-1) // equivalent to `formArray.at(formArray.length - 1)`
```

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No


<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->
Nowadays attempting to retrieve a control in a negative index returns `undefined` (due to underlying usage of native `Array`). This introduces a behavior similar to the ES2021 [`Array.prototype.at()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/at).


## Other information

Consider using the native `Array.prototype.at()` when.

Closes #44642

issue_context.title: forms: Support negative indexes in `FormArray`
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/releated to the feature request?

forms

### Description

Nowadays attempting to retrieve a control in a negative index returns `undefined` (due to underlying usage of native `Array`).
I would like `FormArray` to support relative indexing. Methods like `at()` and `removeAt()` could support negative integers as indexes, which count back from the last item in the array.

### Proposed solution

Similar to the ES2021 [`Array.prototype.at()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/at), support negative integers as indexes:
```ts
 // the following are equivalent:
formArray.at(-1)
formArray.at(formArray.length - 1)
```

Methods which should support relative indexing:
1. `at()`
2. `removeAt()`
3. `insert()`
4. `setControl()`

See proposed solution implementation in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/44631

### Alternatives considered

One could use `formArray.at(formArray.length - 1)` like in indices of native `Array`s pre-ES2021, but this can be exhausting and causes longer lines of code.
comments:
@amitbeck thanks for creating this feature request. According to the Feature Request process ([documented here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/e29eb8abfbfdfb793e08ac88e14b7ba6d2ff2136/docs/GITHUB_PROCESS.md#feature-request-process)), this ticket reached 20 upvotes and we've discussed it with the Angular team.

Given the fact that:
- `FormArray` class represents an Array data structure and using negative indices is common in array methods (such as `splice` and `at`)
- This feature would have minimal impact on the bundle size (we would even be able to pass the index as is in case of `at` function)

We'd like to proceed with this feature request. I'll reopen PR #44631 and provide some feedback there.

Thank you.
